_note: Paper: Video Depth Anything (arXiv 2501.12375). Scaled setup: released VDA-S checkpoint (inference only, no retraining) on hidden procedurally rendered RGB-D corridor videos with exact poses. Paper-reported numbers are kept unchanged below; numbers that have no counterpart in this setup are under keys starting with '_'.

_paper_reported_other._why_not_scored: Parameter count and training-data size cannot be verified from a predictor's outputs, and latency is wall-clock; they are documented constraints (scoring/CONSTRAINTS.md), not scored metrics.

long_video_500.description: Long-video depth on 500-frame hidden corridor videos (the paper's long-video evaluation length). results hold the paper's Table 5 inference-strategy ablation for VDA-S (Baseline = independent windows, window 16; OI+KR = overlap interpolation + key-frame referencing, window 32), means over the paper's real video benchmarks with up to 500 frames. This gym measures the same metrics (same alignment protocol and TAE definition) on procedurally rendered corridor videos, so absolute values are not expected to match; the comparable quantity is the direction of the difference between the two strategies.

absrel.description: Mean absolute relative depth error after one least-squares scale/shift alignment of predicted inverse depth to ground-truth inverse depth shared by the whole video (paper protocol); evaluated on pixels with depth in [0.2, 20].

delta1.description: Fraction of evaluated pixels whose aligned depth is within a factor 1.25 of ground truth (same single per-video alignment).

tae.description: Temporal Alignment Error (paper Eq. 5, x100): aligned depth of each frame is reprojected into the next frame (and back) with the ground-truth camera motion and compared to that frame's aligned depth by AbsRel, averaged over consecutive pairs and both directions.

scale_drift.description: Temporal standard deviation (x100) of the per-frame median log ratio between aligned predicted depth and ground truth: scale jumps between windows and slow scale drift over a long video both raise it.

super_long_video_1500.description: Super-long-video depth on 1500-frame hidden corridor videos, where the scene at the end shares nothing with the start, so a model with a bounded temporal window has to carry one depth scale across dozens of windows. The paper reports no numbers at this length (Fig. 7 is qualitative); results repeat the Table 5 values for orientation only. results hold the paper's Table 5 inference-strategy ablation for VDA-S (Baseline = independent windows, window 16; OI+KR = overlap interpolation + key-frame referencing, window 32), means over the paper's real video benchmarks with up to 500 frames. This gym measures the same metrics (same alignment protocol and TAE definition) on procedurally rendered corridor videos, so absolute values are not expected to match; the comparable quantity is the direction of the difference between the two strategies.

_weights_note: Weights 0.6/0.4: the paper's quantitative long-video protocol is <=500 frames (long_video_500); the super-long setting is its headline claim (consistent depth for minutes-long videos, Fig. 1/7) but has no numeric result, so it gets the smaller weight. Coefficients: absrel, delta1 and tae 1.0 each (the paper's three video metrics, Table 5); scale_drift 0.5 (the paper's drift claim is qualitative and drift also lowers absrel/delta1 under the single per-video alignment).
